jobs.prompt:
chore(cpp): integrate the four runtime-slimming branches into one branch (stage 1b)

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `agent-jobs/cppgw-slim-headers-multipart-20261118-44254409709-1` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi: a known-good state of `cpp/gateway/`, a C++20 port of this repository's TypeScript gateway (`src/`, `serve.ts`), with a JavaScript-style runtime layer (`include/uos/rt`, `src/rt`, `src/runtime`), vendored simdjson and simdutf (`cpp/gateway/third_party/`), and about 442 standalone test binaries (`cpp/gateway/tests/**/*_test.cpp`). On this state the release build passes its whole suite on Linux ARM64. The native gateway is already 1.2-1.9x faster than the TypeScript gateway on Bun end to end and uses about a third of the memory (`cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-perf-request-path-20261117.md`). Every deployment target is 64-bit ARM: an Arch Linux ARM VPS, an Apple Silicon Mac and a Raspberry Pi.

OWNER POLICY (binding): generic functionality comes from mature open-source or standard libraries; exact parity with Bun's quirks and error wording is NOT required; less first-party code is preferred. What must hold: the gateway's functional behaviour (wire formats, status codes, stored data, authentication and validation decisions, accounting) and security never getting weaker.

READ FIRST: `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` (portable build-and-test driver; invoke it as `bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh ...`, the file lacks its executable bit), `cpp/gateway/docs/BUILD.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/RUNTIME.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/OSS-REPLACEMENT-PLAN.md`, `cpp/gateway/PORTING.md` (its coroutine rules are mandatory; its "Host safety" and "compile only through tools/unit.sh" rules apply to the authors' server, not to your disposable runner; where it demands exact Bun parity, the owner policy above wins). `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py <test>` prints a test's application sources; every `src/rt/*.cpp` and the vendored libraries link into every test.

About ten other agents are changing other parts of `cpp/gateway` on their own branches at the same time (URL, HTTP parsing, regex, WebSocket, passkey CBOR and ASN.1, BigInt, date/console/filesystem/env/headers helpers, the stored-value reader, a test-suite repair). You are an INTEGRATOR (see TASK); keep your own edits to what integration needs.

GENERAL RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables. No real provider traffic: use local mocks only.
- Do not edit `.github/` (unless your task says so), the TypeScript, or `cpp/` outside `cpp/gateway/`. Do not delete or weaken tests.
- Model connections can drop: create your report file in the first minutes and commit small steps often (the tree must build at each commit). Leave no build output, binaries or downloads in the checkout.
- Report file: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/<job id>.md`: what you did, exact commands, real counts and measurements, what is unfinished, defects found outside your paths (report, do not fix). End your final message with the same summary.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner (Ubuntu 24.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network). Its packages are too old for this tree: install Clang 21 or newer from apt.llvm.org (or GCC 14+), build Boost 1.92.0 `json` and `container` static libraries from the official source archive in a temp directory (the tree needs Boost >= 1.86), install OpenSSL 3, zlib, ICU, brotli, zstd development packages and build SQLite 3.54.0 as `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` describes. Bun 1.4.0 may be installed when you need to run the TypeScript.

OWNED PATHS
- anything under `cpp/gateway/` that the integration needs. Not `.github/`, not the TypeScript, not `cpp/gateway/third_party/`.

TASK
Four reviewed and accepted branches each slimmed a different part of the JavaScript-style runtime layer, all starting from the same commit (the "small helpers" branch: date, console, filesystem, environment and Headers already on the standard library). You start from one of them, `agent-jobs/cppgw-slim-headers-multipart-20261118-44254409709-1` (Headers storage and inbound multipart). Merge the other three into it with ordinary `git merge` commits (fetch from `origin`):
  1. `agent-jobs/cppgw-slim-console-20261118-44254409709-1` (console formatter)
  2. `agent-jobs/cppgw-slim-env-fs-20261118-44254409709-1` (dotenv parser retired, filesystem/path adapters trimmed)
  3. `agent-jobs/cppgw-slim-containers-gzip-20261118-44254409709-1` (ordered Map/Set emulation, whole-buffer gzip)
Each has a report under `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-slim-*.md`: read them. Conflicts are expected only in shared registries (`fuzz/targets.json`, `docs/DEVIATIONS-FROM-BUN.md`, `tests/LINKS.txt`) and possibly where two branches touched a common caller; resolve keeping each branch's intent. Then:
  a. Build and run the whole suite (release, all shards) and the `asan` configuration for the touched components. This base has THREE known failing application cases that another integration branch already fixes (two expect Bun's legacy date parsing or Headers error text in `tests/claude_code_usage_schema_vectors.inc` / `tests/codex_external_auth_differential_vectors.inc`, one HTTP wire fixture): leave exactly those; everything else must pass.
  b. Check one thing explicitly and write the answer in the report: the dotenv parser was retired. Find every place the gateway's startup, CLIs and tests read configuration (`grep -rn "env" cpp/gateway/runtime cpp/gateway/entrypoints cpp/gateway/src/config* cpp/gateway/src/rt/env.cpp` and the TypeScript `serve.ts`/`src/config*` for comparison) and state whether anything still expects a `.env` file to be loaded implicitly at startup; if the TypeScript service relies on Bun auto-loading `.env` in production, say so clearly, because the operator must then export those variables in the service unit.
Write `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-integrate-s1b-20261118.md`: merges, conflicts and resolutions, the `.env` answer, final counts per shard, first-party production lines in `src/rt` + `src/runtime` before (on your starting commit's parent base) and after.

DONE WHEN
All four release shards pass on your ARM64 runner except exactly the three known cases, `git log` shows the three merges, and the report is complete.
